neighbours.label: a resource or capacity noun right after a verb of having, lacking, getting or giving (have/lack/got/gave the means, the money, the funds, the skills, the know-how, the courage, the equipment, the time to do something), read on the noun; quiet when the resource is not being held by someone (natural resources, tools at a store, 'their resources were stretched'), on 'means' as a verb or in 'by means of', and on ordinary nouns after 'have the' (the book, the right, the feeling)
neighbours.short: resource/capacity someone has or lacks (have the means/skills)
fire: We simply don't have the means to repair the roof this year.
The village lacked the funds to build a new school.
She finally got the courage to ask for a raise.
Do you have the skills to fix a leaking pipe?
The grant gave them the money to hire two more nurses.
He has the know-how to rebuild an engine from scratch.
Our lab lacks the equipment to run those tests.
I never have the time to read anymore.
quiet: The region is rich in natural resources like timber and copper.
The hardware store sells equipment for plumbing and roofing.
Their resources were stretched thin after the long winter.
What does this word mean, and what does it mean here?
The data was sent by means of a secure cable.
Do you have the book I lent you last week?
Every citizen has the right to a fair trial.
I have the feeling it will rain tomorrow.
